statement: Is every bipartite graph without a cycle of length four Sidorenko? That is, if $H$ is a bipartite graph of girth at least six, does $t(H,W) \ge t(K_2,W)^{e(H)}$ hold for every graphon $W$?

source.reference: The 2026 counterexample (openai/math family 161) obtains its deficit only from point pairs that lie in two faces, that is, from 4-cycles of its pattern (its Equation 3.4); Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee (2018, Problem 1.5) ask for the 1-subdivision of every graph, and every such subdivision has girth at least six.

observation: As this record reads the counterexample's coordinate expansion (its Equation 3.4), a point pair contributes a nonconstant term only when it lies in two faces that are both active. In an incidence structure without 4-cycles no pair lies in two faces, so that expansion has no nonconstant term and the construction gives no deficit there. This is a reading of the construction, not a proved lemma, and it does not exclude other mechanisms. The class of bipartite graphs of girth at least six contains every 1-subdivision of a graph and every incidence graph of a linear hypergraph. Known positive members include trees, even cycles, the 1-subdivisions of cliques, of Sidorenko graphs and of graphs with a KNRS-type bound (Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee 2018, Theorems 1.3 and 3.1), and the 1-subdivisions of the graphs of regular polytopes (Conlon and Lee 2017, Theorem 1.1).
neighbours: Is the 1-subdivision of every graph Sidorenko? (Conlon-Kim-Lee-Lee 2018, Problem 1.5)

notes: No conjectured answer is taken; either answer is informative. A counterexample of girth six would need a deficit mechanism other than pairs lying in two faces.
